## Review summary

Created with AI, based on recent reviews

Considering 287 reviews, most reviewers were unhappy with their experience overall. Customers frequently mentioned terrible customer service, noting that support teams were entirely unresponsive, unhelpful, and extremely difficult to reach when urgent problems arose. Consumers also experienced frustrating delays regarding deliveries, completely missing tracking details, and significant troubles when trying to secure prompt refunds for items that malfunctioned.

Some reviewers were happy with the fast shipping, timely delivery, and securely packaged items that arrived in good condition. A few other people also felt that the physical products were of great quality, highly functional, beautifully designed, and very easy to use regularly.See more

What I like most is how easy it is to use. The controls are simple, changing the speed is smooth, and I can start a workout without having to spend ages going through complicated settings. It also runs much quieter than I expected, which is great for home use.

I’ve used it for both walking and jogging and it has handled everything really well so far. The overall build quality feels good and it doesn’t wobble or feel cheap when in use. It’s made exercising at home much more convenient and I’ve definitely been using it more often than I thought I would.

Overall, a really good treadmill that is comfortable, easy to use and feels well made. Very pleased with my purchase.

[**Danferously defective product, poor initial customer service until hauled over social media, and now asking me to delete my honest review. Do not trust this company.**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6aa47625b024daf1d20cbb5a)

Dangerously defective electrics on unboxing.

Dangerous “advice” (gaslighting) that it was “fine”.

That could’ve proved fatal.

Then radio silence.

Then a panicked back-tracking when I shared all this across my Instagram.

Item arrived defective - dangerous uncovered electrical wires hanging out of unit. The PitPat customer service bots said they’d asked their safety team who advised for me to manually pop the exposed copper wiring into the gaping hole, plug the whole thing into the mains, and that this would be “safe”. Despite the wires still being exposed through the large hole to drinks, spills, sweat etc, and the constant fraying of the unprotected electrical wires each time it’s unfolded. Beware the initial helpful “hi there, how can I help?” “Apologies for the inconvenience” empty platitudes… within a couple of messages the chatbots go silent and toddle off. I’ve been lost in chatbot hell for 4 hours, with a highly dangerous item taking up all of my living space, and £200 shortfall.

I am a single parent, working full time in the NHS with no spare income. I bought this to help with my severe chronic pain condition.

And meanwhile, this company can’t fill people’s insta feeds up fast enough with brainless influencer sheep in glossy sports-bras who’ll be sent the only working equipment, in order to flog hundreds of duds via aggressive social media marketing campaigns to unsuspecting marks like me.

Trading standards will be getting a detailed email from me on Monday - these sharks need reporting & investigating.

Gutted I’ve lost £200 of my family’s money at a time when I have very little in the way of finances and am in a lot of physical pain. I work hard for the NHS and as a single-parent-household £200 is a LOT of money for me to waste.

UPDATE:

After creating havoc across Instagram with my exposé of how risky their product and their “advice” had been, I finally had messages from them, reneging on their previous advice, and telling me “Do not touch the item or attempt to turn it on”. No shit, Sherlock!

Once they’d read my review on here & seen my exposing Instagram posts, they agreed to collect the item and have refunded me my money. No goodwill gesture for the 8hrs in total I spent unboxing, downloading, attaching, problem-solving, fruitlessly contacting chatbots, emailing customer services, phoning; then re-boxing (with my own tape / materials), dragging item to porch, and then being back to square one with no treadmill. No goodwill gesture as apology for almost electrocuting me.

No goodwill

No payment for my time and inconvenience.

No apology for their incredibly dangerous advice to poke the exposed electrics back into a metal tube and then use the item.

However - they did email asking me to take this review down, pointing out correctly that they’d been gracious enough to agree me my Statutory Rights to a refund for faulty goods. Therefore this review is updated to reflect this.

Update #2 (27/09/26) - Deer Run have emailed me for a 2nd time asking me to remove my bad review. I won’t be doing, as the nature of my updated review still stands. Defective unsafe item / poor and unsafe initial customer service / only helped because exposed over social media / refunded me as per my statutory rights / no recognition of my wasted hours, packaging materials or stress levels, no goodwill gesture, and now asking me to remove my review based on them doing the bare minimum which they were legally obliged to do as per my statutory rights. My complaint above is objectively fair & accurate - and I won’t be changing it just because DeerRun have graced me with a refund of my own money.

On the one occasion I was eventually able to speak to someone by telephone, I was asked to take photographs of the treadmill as well as photographs of the treadmill with its packaging. I found this request rather unusual, but nevertheless I complied fully and provided the requested photographs in an attempt to resolve the matter.

Overall, I have found the entire experience unnecessarily difficult and frustrating. In my view, there is a significant difference between a product being advertised as capable of running and actually providing a safe, comfortable and satisfactory running experience.

Based on my experience, I would advise potential buyers to carefully consider whether this walking pad is appropriate for their intended use, particularly if they are looking for a treadmill primarily for running rather than occasional walking.

My main concerns are:

• No handrails for running

• No incline function

• Excessive noise during running

• Poor communication and difficulty contacting customer service

• A frustrating and unnecessarily complicated process when trying to resolve the issue

Unfortunately, based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this product for someone looking for a proper running treadmill.

DeerRun has been a blessing in disguise, with cost of living and family of two young children makes gym contracts seem unaffordable of recent - though never say never sure I’ll be back in the gymnasium world of many things great!

Of course a running machine and a self made home gym kit that doesn’t take up too much space saves time on busy family and work routine.

Let’s say a spontaneous decision to purchase the high performance thread-mill due to being an amateur runner as well as qualification in exercise, and for months the advert was appearing and I kept saying to myself now is a good time to start running again, especially after a leg injury that took one year to completely heal with daily strength and stretching.

The design of the product is fold away neatly into the corner - please measure your chosen area of storage to ensure suitability.

The first thing we noticed was the machine has 15% incline and it doesn’t have decline for longer running sessions though that can be overlooked for a high performance runner. My age now being close to 50 years of age the maximum achieved so far is 5.5kph and the machine has the capability of going beyond - not quite sure how fast though should give up to 18 kph.

The weight it can take is 181kg - good for overweight individuals who are looking into transforming their lifestyles and look! The belt is solid and can be adjusted to keep centred with instruction manuals provided, as well as a great customer support team who are always on hand to help. Let’s say better to have a thread mill belt than a gastric belly belt for overweight women and men.

The machine comes with an app called PitPat and you can download on Apple.

The machine is activated by the app and once you activate for the first time you don’t need to use the app unless you want to connect with the running community. You can join forums and challenges online - mostly like an online computer game console.

Overall, so far we have the machine for three months and my energy levels are building up to normal activity, as they should be and have been for the past 25 years until my recent leg injury, though that will be a thing of the past and onto the next challenge for fitness and beyond.

We can honestly recommend DeerRun especially the product named below - money well spent and great for health and wellbeing futures:

DeerRun X20 15% Auto-Incline Foldable Treadmill · Full Running Deck · 18 kph · 181kg Weight Capacity × 1
